categories.main_business_segments: BOOKOFF GROUP HOLDINGS operates three main business segments: (1) Domestic BOOKOFF Business, which includes the operation and franchising of BOOKOFF stores focused on used books and a wide range of reused goods; (2) Premium Services Business, offering high-value reuse services such as luxury brand and jewelry buying/selling through 'hugall', 'aidect', and 'Rehello'; and (3) Overseas Business, which operates BOOKOFF stores in the US and 'Jalan Jalan Japan' reuse stores in Malaysia and Kazakhstan. Additional activities include online retail, trading card specialty stores, and new book stores.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core operational methods center on the procurement of used goods from general consumers, rigorous in-store and online inventory management, and multi-category reuse retailing. It leverages proprietary POS, sales, and inventory management systems, as well as e-commerce platforms for online sales. The group also emphasizes operational efficiency through digital transformation, logistics optimization, and standardized store operations.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Primary customers include general consumers seeking affordable books, media, apparel, and other reused goods, as well as higher-income individuals targeted by premium services for luxury goods and jewelry. The company serves both mass-market and affluent segments, with a growing focus on families, hobbyists, and collectors through specialty stores and online channels.
categories.geographic_coverage: BOOKOFF’s core market is Japan, with a nationwide store network and online presence. Internationally, it operates in the United States (mainly California and New York), Malaysia, and Kazakhstan, with plans for further overseas expansion. The majority of revenue is generated in Japan, but overseas sales are increasing, particularly in Southeast Asia and Central Asia.
categories.supply_chain_position: BOOKOFF operates primarily at the downstream, consumer-facing end of the supply chain as a retailer and franchise operator. It sources inventory directly from consumers through buyback programs and acts as both a buyer and seller of used goods, integrating procurement, processing, and retail sales.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include strengthening the core domestic reuse business, expanding premium and overseas segments, and enhancing digital and operational efficiency. The group is investing in IT systems, e-commerce, logistics, and CRM (notably through its mobile app), while also focusing on sustainability, human capital development, and governance. There is no significant mention of traditional R&D; innovation is mainly in business model, digital transformation, and service enhancement.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated from the sale of used goods (books, media, apparel, luxury items, etc.) through company-operated and franchised stores, as well as online sales. Additional income comes from franchise royalties, premium service fees, and new book sales. The company also earns revenue from value-added services such as jewelry repair and home organization.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: BOOKOFF is a leading player in Japan’s reuse retail industry, positioned as the largest chain for used books and a major multi-category reuse retailer. Key competitors include Hard Off, GEO Holdings, and various regional and online C2C platforms (e.g., Mercari). The company differentiates itself through scale, brand recognition, store network, and a broad product mix.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending May 2025, consolidated sales reached 119.2 billion yen (up 6.8% YoY), with operating profit of 3.4 billion yen and net profit attributable to parent company shareholders of 2.1 billion yen. The company has shown steady revenue and profit growth over recent years, driven by store expansion and diversification, with a workforce of 1,838 employees (plus over 5,000 part-time staff). Overseas and premium segments are growing faster than the domestic core.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: BOOKOFF’s value proposition centers on providing a convenient, trustworthy, and enjoyable reuse shopping experience, with a wide selection of affordable goods and a strong brand. The company emphasizes quality control, customer service, and seamless integration of physical and digital channels. Its premium services target affluent customers with differentiated offerings, while its scale and operational expertise enable competitive pricing and broad product availability.
